about: What `thruline ui` served during a scripted walk over an invented project, in a throwaway HOME with a fresh store; masked. No real session, store or project was read. The T5 and T6 tests read the Change screen, the take-away page and the exported file from it, through the same read path the browser uses (readChange and readPacket, with fetch answered from here).

The walk: a fresh HOME, an invented Cargo project `shop` (one function, `cart_total`, and two tests), one accepted line, then `thruline ui`, headless Chrome at 1512x920. after_pass: Check it again passed, and that run was linked to line 1 (POST /links, as the walk links it). after_fail: `cart_total` was changed so one of its two tests fails and the change was committed; Check it again failed, and that run was linked. after_repass: the change was undone and committed; Check it again passed, and that run was linked.

Each moment holds every GET the Change screen and the take-away page make: the Change, its proposals, coverage (with readiness), the run sheet, inputs, applicability, export, and the explain and claims of the one confirmed conversation. `status`, `exit` and `projection` are the HTTP status and the two X-ThruLine headers as served.

Masked, and nothing else changed: the walk's HOME reads `$HOME`, the walk root `<walk-root>`, the toolchain `<toolchain>`. Every ULID keeps its first ten characters (its time, which is what orders versions) and has its random part replaced by SYNTH and a counter. Every 64- and 40-character hex id is replaced by `cccccccc` and a counter, the same way in every read, so every join (evidence id, binding id, run key, snapshot) still holds.

The /findings read of each moment was added at the A3 integration merge (integrate 6), not captured on the walk: the walk ran on a build before that route (T-4-2), and the merged Change screen and take-away page read it too. The walk ran no review, so each is what the merged `thruline ui` serves for a Change with no reviews - its shape taken from that build serving a fresh setup.sh store - with change_id this capture's, and current_revision and masking copied from the same moment's Change document, which the server fills from the same record (decisions.target_revision; the same masking treatment).

The /api/licence read of each moment was added at the A2 merge of dist/release-and-licence onto the integration (int-dq), not captured on the walk: the walk ran on a build before that route (T-DIST-4), and the merged Change screen reads it too (readChange, so Approve can say why it is off). It is the document the merged `thruline ui` serves in a fresh HOME with the paid gate off and no licence key built in, the same at every moment because it reads no ledger row: status 200, no X-ThruLine headers, a body with no path, id or fingerprint in it.

inputs_other_folder_state.plain: This was checked on the same commit, in the same folder, and the folder was not set up the same way, so it isn't counted.

inputs_other_revision.plain: This was checked on different code than this Change is set up against.
inputs_other_revision.technical: The examined base revision differs from the candidate's.

prepare_not_written_down.technical: The field is SQL NULL: the probe did not answer, and nothing was substituted for it.

accept_edit_not_selected.plain: You rewrote line {count} but did not choose it, so nothing would have been saved. Choose it, or drop the rewrite.
accept_edit_not_selected.technical: An edit was supplied for a number outside the selection. Refused rather than dropped, because a dropped edit is a person's words silently discarded.

accept_is_not_approval.plain: Agreeing what counts as done is not approving the work. Nobody has approved anything.
accept_is_not_approval.technical: `B5.7`: an acceptance is a row in `change_scope_acceptances` naming an actor, a time, a version and a rationale. No decision or approval record exists yet, and this act does not touch one.

accept_needs_a_criterion.plain: There is nothing to accept. An empty list is not a list of what counts as done.
accept_needs_a_criterion.technical: The selection resolved to zero criteria. An empty `criteria_json` would be a scope version that every later examination passes vacuously, which is worse than having none.

accept_needs_actor.plain: We cannot write down what counts as done without a name. Say who is accepting it.
accept_needs_actor.technical: `change_scope_acceptances.accepted_by` is `NOT NULL` with a non-empty CHECK. This is that refusal in words, said before the store is opened.

accept_nothing_new.plain: This is already what counts as done, version {version}. There is nothing new to accept.
accept_nothing_new.technical: The resulting five scope lists hash to the same `content_sha256` as the standing version. A version that changes nothing would still consume one of the bounded slots and would make the history harder to read.

accept_unknown_criterion.plain: There is no line numbered {count} to accept.
accept_unknown_criterion.technical: The number is outside the set this reading proposed. Refused rather than ignored: silently skipping it would save a shorter list than the one that was chosen.

accept_version_limit.plain: This Change already holds {lists} of what counts as done, which is the most we keep ({version}). Open a new Change for a new direction.
accept_version_limit.technical: `change_scope_revisions` is append-only, so the series only grows. The bound is stated on every reading before it is reached, and the refusal names what to do instead.

accept_would_overwrite_your_words.plain: This would put our wording back over {lines} you wrote yourself. Nothing was saved. Say plainly that you are replacing them, and it will be.
accept_would_overwrite_your_words.technical: {count} lines of accepted version {version} match no proposal this store derives, so they are the accepting actor's own text, and the list about to be written does not contain them. Refused: `replacing` makes it an explicit act (`B5.5`).

accept_would_weaken.plain: This would drop {lines} you already accepted, or replace one with something that says less. Nothing was saved. Say plainly that you are replacing them, and it will be.
accept_would_weaken.technical: Comparing the list about to be written against accepted version {version} with the same two tests a re-proposal gets — a dropped negation, and a word set that is a proper subset — found {count} accepted lines dropped or weakened. Refused; `replacing` makes it an explicit act instead of a silent one (`B5.5`).

accept_written.plain: Saved as what counts as done, version {version} — {items}.
accept_written.technical: Appended scope revision {version} with {count} criteria and an acceptance record carrying actor, time, version and rationale (`B5.6`). Every earlier version is unchanged and still readable.

accepted_scope_none.plain: Nobody has written down what counts as done for this Change yet.
accepted_scope_none.technical: No `change_scope_revisions` row exists for this Change. Shown as missing, never as agreed, and never filled in for you.

check_advisory.plain: Worth running. Not needed before approval.
check_advisory.technical: Advisory in this profile: its absence never blocks a decision, and its presence is not a substitute for a mandatory check.

check_mandatory.plain: Needed before this can be approved.
check_mandatory.technical: Mandatory in this profile. If it cannot run on this machine it stays on the list and stays needed — `B5.10` forbids dropping it.

check_needs_a_recipe.plain: Installed here, but there is no reviewed settings file for it yet ({name}), so it cannot run.
check_needs_a_recipe.technical: The program is on `PATH`, and `{name}` does not exist. Every adapter needs explicit reviewed sources or targets before it may run; an adapter with no settings file would be examining something nobody chose.

check_not_available_here.technical: `{name}` is not on `PATH` on this machine. The check stays on the list, because a dropped check looks exactly like a passed one to anybody reading the list later.

check_ready.technical: The program is on `PATH` and the project holds a reviewed settings file for it. Being able to run is still not having run.

criterion_as_proposed.technical: The accepted text matches a criterion this store's proposer derives, word for word once whitespace and case are normalised.

criterion_not_observable_as_written.plain: As you wrote it, we cannot tell what would satisfy this. It is kept exactly as you wrote it.
criterion_not_observable_as_written.technical: The accepted line does not cut into the three parts. It is stored unchanged and shown with this line beside it: your list is yours, and a tool that quietly rewrote it would be worse than one that says it cannot read it.

criterion_your_words.plain: Not in the words we proposed — this is how you wrote it.
criterion_your_words.technical: The accepted text matches no proposal this store derives now, so it is attributed to the actor on the acceptance record. If the proposer's own rules change, a line accepted earlier can move into this class; that direction is the safe one, because the tool never claims authorship of words it did not write.

note_fragment.plain: Kept as a note, not something to check: this is a piece of a sentence, not a whole one, so it cannot say what would count as done.
note_fragment.technical: The span does not read as a whole sentence — it begins mid-line in lower case, or it ends without a terminal stop — so it is never offered as a criterion whatever shape it has. Kept verbatim (`T-2-8-F1`).

note_masked.plain: Kept as a note, not something to check: part of this looked like a secret, so it was replaced before we showed it, and these are no longer your exact words.
note_masked.technical: The masked text carries a `[masked: …]` marker. Masking runs before the cut, and a mask can consume a sentence terminator with the secret; proposing the result would be proposing a sentence nobody wrote. Kept as the masked text, verbatim.

note_no_condition.plain: Kept as a note, not something to check: it does not say when it should hold.
note_no_condition.technical: An outcome was found, but no condition word in front of it with a subject before that, so the sentence as written holds always. Kept verbatim.

note_no_outcome.plain: Kept as a note, not something to check: it does not say what you would see if it were done.
note_no_outcome.technical: No word in the sentence matched the closed outcome table (`change_propose::OUTCOME_MARKERS`), so there is nothing a check could observe. Kept verbatim; nothing was invented to fill the gap.

note_no_subject.plain: Kept as a note, not something to check: it does not say what it is about.
note_no_subject.technical: The span before the condition carried no word outside the stopword list, so the sentence has no subject to check anything against. Kept verbatim.

note_too_long.plain: Kept as a note, not something to check: it is a paragraph, and a paragraph is not one thing to check.
note_too_long.technical: The sentence is longer than `change_propose::MAX_CRITERION_CHARS`. Splitting it would mean choosing which half was meant, which is the invention this proposer refuses. Kept verbatim.

profile_is_not_evidence.plain: A list of checks is not evidence. Nothing here has run yet, so everything here still needs evidence.
profile_is_not_evidence.technical: `B5.10`: a suggested profile is a plan for what to examine. Suggesting it creates no check row, no run and no outcome, and nothing in this list may be read as a result.

profile_no_paths.plain: The record does not show which files this work touched, so we cannot say what kind of work it is or what to check.
profile_no_paths.technical: No confirmed session had a readable changed path and the standing scope lists none, so the change-type inference had no input. Missing input is stated rather than guessed at.

proposal_none.plain: We could not turn anything in the record into a line you could check. What we found is kept below, in your own words.
proposal_none.technical: No sentence in the Change's purpose, the original prompt, or any confirmed session's opening request carried all three parts of the shape. An empty set is an answer, not a failure: every sentence is listed as a note naming the part it was missing.

proposal_reasoning.plain: This is your own wording from the start of this work, cut down to the part someone could check.
proposal_reasoning.technical: Cut from one request's text at a sentence boundary and matched against the subject · condition · observable-outcome shape. The source request id and the character span travel with it; no word was added, removed or rephrased.

reproposal_changes_nothing.plain: Reading the record again changes nothing you accepted. Only you can change that, and only by accepting a new list.
reproposal_changes_nothing.technical: `propose` performs no write. The standing version, its acceptance record and its digest are untouched by any number of readings.

reproposal_removed.plain: You accepted this, and nothing in the record proposes it now. It stays accepted until you say otherwise.
reproposal_removed.technical: No proposal in this reading pairs with this accepted line by subject. Reading again cannot remove an accepted line; only a new acceptance can replace the list.

reproposal_restated.plain: The same thing in different words as a line you already accepted. Nothing changes.
reproposal_restated.technical: The paired proposal differs in wording but fails both weakening tests. It is listed so the difference is visible, and it changes nothing.

reproposal_weakened.plain: This new wording says less than the line you already accepted. We are not replacing the stronger one.
reproposal_weakened.technical: The paired proposal either drops a negation the accepted line carries, or its word set is a proper subset of the accepted line's. Both are named as weakenings and neither is applied (`B5.5`).

scope_from_the_work.plain: These are the folders the work already confirmed for this Change touched. Accepting them with what counts as done is what lets later checks be counted for it.
scope_from_the_work.technical: Each entry is the directory of a path one confirmed session changed, spelled as a `dir/**` subtree the scope matcher understands, with entries covered by a shorter one removed. Derived at read from stored rows; nothing on disk is inspected.

scope_none_found.plain: The record does not show which files the work for this Change changed, so there are no folders to cover yet. Confirm the work that belongs to this Change, and they will be proposed here.
scope_none_found.technical: No file-editing tool call with a readable path was found in any confirmed session, so the allowed scope is proposed as empty rather than as the whole project. An empty answer is an answer, never a wildcard.

scope_over_the_bound.plain: {count} more folders were left off this list, which is kept to {version} so it stays something you can read before you accept it.
scope_over_the_bound.technical: The derived entry list exceeded `change_propose::MAX_SCOPE_PATHS`; the remainder is counted here rather than dropped silently. Accepting more is a re-scope with the folders named.

scope_versions_bounded.plain: {lists} of what counts as done so far. We keep at most {version}.
scope_versions_bounded.technical: `COUNT(*)` over this Change's `change_scope_revisions` rows, against `change_propose::MAX_SCOPE_VERSIONS`. Both numbers are shown so the bound is visible before it refuses anything.

type_authorization_sensitive.plain: This work touches who is allowed to do what, so it is worth being careful.
type_authorization_sensitive.technical: A changed path names authorization, a credential or a policy. The profile adds a mandatory static examination; it does not claim the work is unsafe.

type_backend_behaviour.plain: This work changes what the program does behind the screen.
type_backend_behaviour.technical: No changed path matched a narrower kind, so the work is treated as program behaviour and the profile asks for the project's own tests.

type_data_schema.plain: This work changes how stored things are shaped, so what happens to things already stored is part of what counts as done.
type_data_schema.technical: A changed path names a migration, a schema or a `.sql` file. A schema change with no compatibility examination is the one class this product will not read as finished.

type_documentation.plain: This work is mostly writing, not behaviour.
type_documentation.technical: One or more changed paths is a document by extension or directory. `B5.14`: opening a document proves nothing about behaviour.

type_interface_behaviour.plain: This work changes what someone using the product sees or does.
type_interface_behaviour.technical: Changed paths include interface sources or a route. The examinations worth running are the ones that drive the interface, not the ones that read it.

examination_none_yet.sentence: Nothing has been checked for this Change yet.

rejected_link.sentence: You said this work does not belong to this Change.

request.sentence: What was asked for, in the words it was asked in, and who asked.

scope_acceptance.sentence: Agreeing what counts as done is not approving the work itself.

suggested.sentence: We think this belongs here. Nothing is carried over until you say it does.

accept_edit_not_selected.plain: You rewrote line {count} but did not choose it, so nothing would have been saved. Choose it, or drop the rewrite.
accept_edit_not_selected.technical: An edit was supplied for a number outside the selection. Refused rather than dropped, because a dropped edit is a person's words silently discarded.

accept_is_not_approval.plain: Agreeing what counts as done is not approving the work. Nobody has approved anything.
accept_is_not_approval.technical: `B5.7`: an acceptance is a row in `change_scope_acceptances` naming an actor, a time, a version and a rationale. No decision or approval record exists yet, and this act does not touch one.

accept_needs_a_criterion.plain: There is nothing to accept. An empty list is not a list of what counts as done.
accept_needs_a_criterion.technical: The selection resolved to zero criteria. An empty `criteria_json` would be a scope version that every later examination passes vacuously, which is worse than having none.

accept_needs_actor.plain: We cannot write down what counts as done without a name. Say who is accepting it.
accept_needs_actor.technical: `change_scope_acceptances.accepted_by` is `NOT NULL` with a non-empty CHECK. This is that refusal in words, said before the store is opened.

accept_nothing_new.plain: This is already what counts as done, version {version}. There is nothing new to accept.
accept_nothing_new.technical: The resulting five scope lists hash to the same `content_sha256` as the standing version. A version that changes nothing would still consume one of the bounded slots and would make the history harder to read.

accept_unknown_criterion.plain: There is no line numbered {count} to accept.
accept_unknown_criterion.technical: The number is outside the set this reading proposed. Refused rather than ignored: silently skipping it would save a shorter list than the one that was chosen.

accept_version_limit.plain: This Change already holds {lists} of what counts as done, which is the most we keep ({version}). Open a new Change for a new direction.
accept_version_limit.technical: `change_scope_revisions` is append-only, so the series only grows. The bound is stated on every reading before it is reached, and the refusal names what to do instead.

accept_would_overwrite_your_words.plain: This would put our wording back over {lines} you wrote yourself. Nothing was saved. Say plainly that you are replacing them, and it will be.
accept_would_overwrite_your_words.technical: {count} lines of accepted version {version} match no proposal this store derives, so they are the accepting actor's own text, and the list about to be written does not contain them. Refused: `replacing` makes it an explicit act (`B5.5`).

accept_would_weaken.plain: This would drop {lines} you already accepted, or replace one with something that says less. Nothing was saved. Say plainly that you are replacing them, and it will be.
accept_would_weaken.technical: Comparing the list about to be written against accepted version {version} with the same two tests a re-proposal gets — a dropped negation, and a word set that is a proper subset — found {count} accepted lines dropped or weakened. Refused; `replacing` makes it an explicit act instead of a silent one (`B5.5`).

accept_written.plain: Saved as what counts as done, version {version} — {items}.
accept_written.technical: Appended scope revision {version} with {count} criteria and an acceptance record carrying actor, time, version and rationale (`B5.6`). Every earlier version is unchanged and still readable.

accepted_scope_none.plain: Nobody has written down what counts as done for this Change yet.
accepted_scope_none.technical: No `change_scope_revisions` row exists for this Change. Shown as missing, never as agreed, and never filled in for you.

check_advisory.plain: Worth running. Not needed before approval.
check_advisory.technical: Advisory in this profile: its absence never blocks a decision, and its presence is not a substitute for a mandatory check.

check_mandatory.plain: Needed before this can be approved.
check_mandatory.technical: Mandatory in this profile. If it cannot run on this machine it stays on the list and stays needed — `B5.10` forbids dropping it.

check_needs_a_recipe.plain: Installed here, but there is no reviewed settings file for it yet ({name}), so it cannot run.
check_needs_a_recipe.technical: The program is on `PATH`, and `{name}` does not exist. Every adapter needs explicit reviewed sources or targets before it may run; an adapter with no settings file would be examining something nobody chose.

check_not_available_here.technical: `{name}` is not on `PATH` on this machine. The check stays on the list, because a dropped check looks exactly like a passed one to anybody reading the list later.

check_ready.technical: The program is on `PATH` and the project holds a reviewed settings file for it. Being able to run is still not having run.

criterion_as_proposed.technical: The accepted text matches a criterion this store's proposer derives, word for word once whitespace and case are normalised.

criterion_not_observable_as_written.plain: As you wrote it, we cannot tell what would satisfy this. It is kept exactly as you wrote it.
criterion_not_observable_as_written.technical: The accepted line does not cut into the three parts. It is stored unchanged and shown with this line beside it: your list is yours, and a tool that quietly rewrote it would be worse than one that says it cannot read it.

criterion_your_words.plain: Not in the words we proposed — this is how you wrote it.
criterion_your_words.technical: The accepted text matches no proposal this store derives now, so it is attributed to the actor on the acceptance record. If the proposer's own rules change, a line accepted earlier can move into this class; that direction is the safe one, because the tool never claims authorship of words it did not write.

readiness_needs_evidence.technical: {n} obligations have outcome `needs_evidence`. Readiness is false; each obligation and its class is listed below.

readiness_needs_evidence_one.technical: One obligation has outcome `needs_evidence`. Readiness is false; the obligation and its class are listed below.

readiness_no_exception_path.plain: Nothing can be set aside on this Change: what counts as done for it does not say who is allowed to do that. Say so in what counts as done first, naming who decides.
readiness_no_exception_path.technical: `B7.21`: the accepted check profile carries no `policy:exceptions-allowed-by:<authority>` entry, so `change_readiness::exception_authority` is `None` and both write routes refuse. The authority is never taken from the request.

readiness_not_applicable.plain: Doesn't apply here — {why} (said by {who}, under {authority}). Nobody checked this.
readiness_not_applicable.technical: An appended waiver record of kind `not_applicable` — the record says it does not apply — with actor, authority and rationale. Same treatment as a waiver: it clears the obligation and is never evidence.

readiness_not_proven.plain: The record holds the opposite of this.
readiness_not_proven.technical: A bearing item observed `not_proven` (non-zero exit with both streams captured whole).

readiness_not_waivable.plain: This one can't be set aside by anybody.
readiness_not_waivable.technical: `B7.12`: candidate identity, decision authority and packet consistency are refused by `ObligationWaiver::validate`, so no stored record can set them aside.

readiness_nothing_accepted.plain: Nothing counts as done yet, so nothing is ready. Say what counts as done for this Change first.
readiness_nothing_accepted.technical: `B7.7`: no accepted scope version, or an accepted scope with no criteria. An empty obligation set is never satisfied vacuously; readiness is refused before any other condition is read.

readiness_nothing_looked.technical: Coverage state `none`: no link row bears on this criterion. Absence of evidence, recorded as absence.

readiness_other_version.plain: What was checked was a different version of the code.
readiness_other_version.technical: `applies` is not `true` for every bearing item: the examined-inputs record of each does not match the Change's intended record. A result about another version is a result about something else.

readiness_ready.plain: Ready for approval for version {version}. It rests on:
readiness_ready.technical: `change_readiness::compute` returned ready for {version}: an accepted scope with at least one criterion, an examined-inputs record for the candidate, and one admissible item per criterion obligation. The list below is `rests_on`.

readiness_ready_with_exceptions.plain: Ready for approval with exceptions for version {version}. It rests on:
readiness_ready_with_exceptions.technical: `change_readiness::compute` returned ready for {version} with `with_exceptions` set: every obligation clears, and at least one of them clears on an appended waiver record rather than on an admissible item. `rests_on` holds only the satisfied ones; the set-aside lines are listed separately and are in neither.

readiness_review_missing.plain: What counts as done for this Change says it needs a review, and no review is written down.
readiness_review_missing.technical: The accepted check profile carries a review policy entry and no review record exists. Recorded, never assumed: with no such entry there is no review obligation at all.

readiness_settled_nothing.plain: Something ran, and it settled nothing about this.
readiness_settled_nothing.technical: Coverage state `ran_nothing`, or every bearing item observed `loose`: linked, and nothing in it satisfies the line.

readiness_stale.plain: This was checked, and the files it looked at have changed since.
readiness_stale.technical: An applicability row says `no_longer_applies` for a bearing item. Freshness outranks the observed result.

readiness_stopped.plain: The check that covers this was stopped before it finished.
readiness_stopped.technical: A bearing item's latest `change_run_executions` row is `running`, `cancelled`, `interrupted` or `blocked`. `settles` is false for all four (T-3-4).

readiness_tool_absent.plain: The check this asks for can't run on this machine.
readiness_tool_absent.technical: Coverage state `absent_tool`: the accepted profile asks for a class whose program was not resolvable here. Not a failure of the check — the check cannot start.

readiness_unknown.plain: Something ran, and ThruLine can't tell what it covered.
readiness_unknown.technical: Observed `couldnt`: a test command exited 0 and this store holds no count of what it ran, so a full suite, zero tests and every test skipped are indistinguishable (`Q3`).

readiness_waived.plain: Waived by {who}, under {authority}: {why}. Nobody checked this.
readiness_waived.technical: An appended waiver record of kind `waived` with actor, authority and rationale. It stops the obligation blocking and is never counted as evidence: it is absent from `rests_on` by construction.

inputs_applies.plain: Checked on the code this Change is set up against.
inputs_applies.technical: The examined-inputs record's base revision, source identity (wsid1, which covers uncommitted changes) and worktree path equal the candidate's, and where a running application was examined its port owner and database match the ones this Change names.

inputs_missing.plain: Nothing says what was looked at here, so this isn't counted.
inputs_missing.technical: No `examination_inputs` row exists for this examination. An examination with no examined-inputs record cannot be shown to be about any version, so it is attached to no criterion's conclusion.

inputs_no_app_named.plain: This came from a running copy of the app, and this Change doesn't say which running copy it is about.
inputs_no_app_named.technical: The examination carries a `running_app` target and the intended record carries `none`. Nothing is inferred from the absence.

inputs_nothing_bound.plain: This Change is not set up to check against your code yet, so nothing here can say whether a run was about it.
inputs_nothing_bound.technical: No `examination_inputs` row with subject kind `intended` exists for this Change, so no examination can be compared against it and every item's applicability is null rather than false. Changes opened on this build are bound when they are opened; this one predates that.

inputs_other_app.plain: This came from a different running copy of the app.
inputs_other_app.technical: The examined port, or the executable of the process owning the listening socket, differs from the one this Change names.

inputs_other_database.plain: This came from a copy of the app using a different database.
inputs_other_database.technical: The port owner matches and the database file the process has open differs from the one this Change names.

inputs_other_edits.plain: This was checked on the same commit, with different unsaved changes.
inputs_other_edits.technical: The base revisions, worktree paths are equal, at least one side reports uncommitted changes, and the source identities (wsid1, covering staged, dirty, deleted, renamed and untracked files) are not equal.

inputs_other_folder_state.plain: This was checked on the same commit, in the same folder, and the folder was not set up the same way, so it isn't counted.
inputs_other_folder_state.technical: The base revisions and worktree paths are equal, neither side reports uncommitted changes, and the source identities (wsid1) still differ — the branch name, a submodule's checked-out head, the sparse-checkout file, an LFS attribute or a re-created git dir are all inside that digest. Reported separately so the edits sentence is never said about two clean trees (T-3-2b).

inputs_other_revision.plain: This was checked on different code than this Change is set up against.
inputs_other_revision.technical: The examined base revision differs from the candidate's.

inputs_other_worktree.plain: This is a second checkout of the same commit. ThruLine records one checkout per Change — pick the one you're working in.
inputs_other_worktree.technical: The base revisions are equal and the examined worktree path differs from the candidate's. Asked before the source identity, which contains the root and git common dir and would otherwise report a clean sibling checkout as an edits difference (T-3-2b).

inputs_record_count.technical: {count} in `examination_inputs` for this examination, newest standing.

inputs_unknown_app.plain: We can't tell which running copy of the app this came from, so it isn't counted.
inputs_unknown_app.technical: The listening port's owning executable or the database path is `unknown` on one side; `lsof` did not answer.

inputs_unknown_is_not_a_value.plain: We can't write down "unknown" as if it were an answer. Leave it out instead.
inputs_unknown_is_not_a_value.technical: A caller passed the literal string `unknown` as a field value. The module refuses it before the store is touched, and the CHECK constraints refuse it again.

inputs_unknown_version.plain: We can't tell which code this was checked on, so it isn't counted.
inputs_unknown_version.technical: The base revision or the source identity is `unknown` on one side. Unknown never compares equal, including to another unknown.

inputs_unknown_worktree.plain: We can't tell which copy of your project folder this was checked in, so it isn't counted.
inputs_unknown_worktree.technical: The worktree path is `unknown` on one side.

prepare_app_unknown.plain: Nothing is running on port {port} that we could identify.
prepare_app_unknown.technical: `lsof` returned no owning pid for port {port}, so the owner's executable and database are recorded as unknown.

prepare_base.technical: The base revision (git HEAD) the examined-inputs record carries.

prepare_not_written_down.technical: The field is SQL NULL: the probe did not answer, and nothing was substituted for it.

prepare_nothing_recorded.plain: Nothing is written down yet about what will be looked at for this Change. Run `thruline change prepare` and it will be.
prepare_nothing_recorded.technical: No `examination_inputs` row with subject kind `intended` exists for this change id.

prepare_repository.technical: The examined worktree path, from the workspace identity's canonical root.

prepare_running_app.plain: The app running on port {port}, started by {app}.
prepare_running_app.technical: The process owning the listening socket on port {port}: executable {app}, read with `lsof -nP -sTCP:LISTEN` and `ps -o comm=`.

prepare_tool_absent.plain: {tool} is not on this machine, so it will not run.
prepare_tool_absent.technical: {tool} could not be executed here. The check stays listed and stays required; nothing is marked done because the tool is missing.

prepare_tool_present.technical: {tool} answered `--version` with {value} at the moment the record was written.

prepare_tool_version_unknown.plain: {tool} will run. It does not say which version it is.
prepare_tool_version_unknown.technical: {tool} is on PATH and its `--version` produced nothing readable. Recorded as unknown, never guessed.

prepare_uncommitted_included.technical: The source identity covers {count} staged, dirty, deleted, renamed or untracked entries, and the snapshot's dirty-diff digest is recorded beside it.

prepare_uncommitted_none.plain: There are no unsaved changes: this is exactly what is committed.
prepare_uncommitted_none.technical: The workspace observation found no staged, dirty, deleted, renamed or untracked entry.

prepare_uncommitted_unknown.plain: We could not read whether you have unsaved changes.
prepare_uncommitted_unknown.technical: The workspace observation was incomplete, so no source identity was minted. Recorded as unknown; never assumed clean.

accepted_scope.sentence: The list this work will be judged against.

association.sentence: A piece of the record that someone or something says belongs here.

change.sentence: One bounded piece of work you are being asked to accept.

confirmed.sentence: You said this belongs to this Change.

decision_none_yet.sentence: Nobody has approved this or asked for changes.

examination_none_yet.sentence: Nothing has been checked for this Change yet.

implementation.sentence: The project and the one exact version of the work this is about.

rejected_link.sentence: You said this work does not belong to this Change.

request.sentence: What was asked for, in the words it was asked in, and who asked.

scope_acceptance.sentence: Agreeing what counts as done is not approving the work itself.

suggested.sentence: We think this belongs here. Nothing is carried over until you say it does.

accept_edit_not_selected.plain: You rewrote line {count} but did not choose it, so nothing would have been saved. Choose it, or drop the rewrite.
accept_edit_not_selected.technical: An edit was supplied for a number outside the selection. Refused rather than dropped, because a dropped edit is a person's words silently discarded.

accept_is_not_approval.plain: Agreeing what counts as done is not approving the work. Nobody has approved anything.
accept_is_not_approval.technical: `B5.7`: an acceptance is a row in `change_scope_acceptances` naming an actor, a time, a version and a rationale. No decision or approval record exists yet, and this act does not touch one.

accept_needs_a_criterion.plain: There is nothing to accept. An empty list is not a list of what counts as done.
accept_needs_a_criterion.technical: The selection resolved to zero criteria. An empty `criteria_json` would be a scope version that every later examination passes vacuously, which is worse than having none.

accept_needs_actor.plain: We cannot write down what counts as done without a name. Say who is accepting it.
accept_needs_actor.technical: `change_scope_acceptances.accepted_by` is `NOT NULL` with a non-empty CHECK. This is that refusal in words, said before the store is opened.

accept_nothing_new.plain: This is already what counts as done, version {version}. There is nothing new to accept.
accept_nothing_new.technical: The resulting five scope lists hash to the same `content_sha256` as the standing version. A version that changes nothing would still consume one of the bounded slots and would make the history harder to read.

accept_unknown_criterion.plain: There is no line numbered {count} to accept.
accept_unknown_criterion.technical: The number is outside the set this reading proposed. Refused rather than ignored: silently skipping it would save a shorter list than the one that was chosen.

accept_version_limit.plain: This Change already holds {lists} of what counts as done, which is the most we keep ({version}). Open a new Change for a new direction.
accept_version_limit.technical: `change_scope_revisions` is append-only, so the series only grows. The bound is stated on every reading before it is reached, and the refusal names what to do instead.

accept_would_overwrite_your_words.plain: This would put our wording back over {lines} you wrote yourself. Nothing was saved. Say plainly that you are replacing them, and it will be.
accept_would_overwrite_your_words.technical: {count} lines of accepted version {version} match no proposal this store derives, so they are the accepting actor's own text, and the list about to be written does not contain them. Refused: `replacing` makes it an explicit act (`B5.5`).

accept_would_weaken.plain: This would drop {lines} you already accepted, or replace one with something that says less. Nothing was saved. Say plainly that you are replacing them, and it will be.
accept_would_weaken.technical: Comparing the list about to be written against accepted version {version} with the same two tests a re-proposal gets — a dropped negation, and a word set that is a proper subset — found {count} accepted lines dropped or weakened. Refused; `replacing` makes it an explicit act instead of a silent one (`B5.5`).

accept_written.plain: Saved as what counts as done, version {version} — {items}.
accept_written.technical: Appended scope revision {version} with {count} criteria and an acceptance record carrying actor, time, version and rationale (`B5.6`). Every earlier version is unchanged and still readable.

accepted_scope_none.plain: Nobody has written down what counts as done for this Change yet.
accepted_scope_none.technical: No `change_scope_revisions` row exists for this Change. Shown as missing, never as agreed, and never filled in for you.

check_advisory.plain: Worth running. Not needed before approval.
check_advisory.technical: Advisory in this profile: its absence never blocks a decision, and its presence is not a substitute for a mandatory check.

check_mandatory.plain: Needed before this can be approved.
check_mandatory.technical: Mandatory in this profile. If it cannot run on this machine it stays on the list and stays needed — `B5.10` forbids dropping it.

check_needs_a_recipe.plain: Installed here, but there is no reviewed settings file for it yet ({name}), so it cannot run.
check_needs_a_recipe.technical: The program is on `PATH`, and `{name}` does not exist. Every adapter needs explicit reviewed sources or targets before it may run; an adapter with no settings file would be examining something nobody chose.

check_not_available_here.technical: `{name}` is not on `PATH` on this machine. The check stays on the list, because a dropped check looks exactly like a passed one to anybody reading the list later.

check_ready.technical: The program is on `PATH` and the project holds a reviewed settings file for it. Being able to run is still not having run.

criterion_as_proposed.technical: The accepted text matches a criterion this store's proposer derives, word for word once whitespace and case are normalised.

criterion_not_observable_as_written.plain: As you wrote it, we cannot tell what would satisfy this. It is kept exactly as you wrote it.
criterion_not_observable_as_written.technical: The accepted line does not cut into the three parts. It is stored unchanged and shown with this line beside it: your list is yours, and a tool that quietly rewrote it would be worse than one that says it cannot read it.

criterion_your_words.plain: Not in the words we proposed — this is how you wrote it.
criterion_your_words.technical: The accepted text matches no proposal this store derives now, so it is attributed to the actor on the acceptance record. If the proposer's own rules change, a line accepted earlier can move into this class; that direction is the safe one, because the tool never claims authorship of words it did not write.

note_fragment.plain: Kept as a note, not something to check: this is a piece of a sentence, not a whole one, so it cannot say what would count as done.
note_fragment.technical: The span does not read as a whole sentence — it begins mid-line in lower case, or it ends without a terminal stop — so it is never offered as a criterion whatever shape it has. Kept verbatim (`T-2-8-F1`).

note_masked.plain: Kept as a note, not something to check: part of this looked like a secret, so it was replaced before we showed it, and these are no longer your exact words.
note_masked.technical: The masked text carries a `[masked: …]` marker. Masking runs before the cut, and a mask can consume a sentence terminator with the secret; proposing the result would be proposing a sentence nobody wrote. Kept as the masked text, verbatim.

note_no_condition.plain: Kept as a note, not something to check: it does not say when it should hold.
note_no_condition.technical: An outcome was found, but no condition word in front of it with a subject before that, so the sentence as written holds always. Kept verbatim.

note_no_outcome.plain: Kept as a note, not something to check: it does not say what you would see if it were done.
note_no_outcome.technical: No word in the sentence matched the closed outcome table (`change_propose::OUTCOME_MARKERS`), so there is nothing a check could observe. Kept verbatim; nothing was invented to fill the gap.

note_no_subject.plain: Kept as a note, not something to check: it does not say what it is about.
note_no_subject.technical: The span before the condition carried no word outside the stopword list, so the sentence has no subject to check anything against. Kept verbatim.

note_too_long.plain: Kept as a note, not something to check: it is a paragraph, and a paragraph is not one thing to check.
note_too_long.technical: The sentence is longer than `change_propose::MAX_CRITERION_CHARS`. Splitting it would mean choosing which half was meant, which is the invention this proposer refuses. Kept verbatim.

profile_is_not_evidence.plain: A list of checks is not evidence. Nothing here has run yet, so everything here still needs evidence.
profile_is_not_evidence.technical: `B5.10`: a suggested profile is a plan for what to examine. Suggesting it creates no check row, no run and no outcome, and nothing in this list may be read as a result.

profile_no_paths.plain: The record does not show which files this work touched, so we cannot say what kind of work it is or what to check.
profile_no_paths.technical: No confirmed session had a readable changed path and the standing scope lists none, so the change-type inference had no input. Missing input is stated rather than guessed at.

proposal_none.plain: We could not turn anything in the record into a line you could check. What we found is kept below, in your own words.
proposal_none.technical: No sentence in the Change's purpose, the original prompt, or any confirmed session's opening request carried all three parts of the shape. An empty set is an answer, not a failure: every sentence is listed as a note naming the part it was missing.

proposal_reasoning.plain: This is your own wording from the start of this work, cut down to the part someone could check.
proposal_reasoning.technical: Cut from one request's text at a sentence boundary and matched against the subject · condition · observable-outcome shape. The source request id and the character span travel with it; no word was added, removed or rephrased.

reproposal_changes_nothing.plain: Reading the record again changes nothing you accepted. Only you can change that, and only by accepting a new list.
reproposal_changes_nothing.technical: `propose` performs no write. The standing version, its acceptance record and its digest are untouched by any number of readings.

reproposal_removed.plain: You accepted this, and nothing in the record proposes it now. It stays accepted until you say otherwise.
reproposal_removed.technical: No proposal in this reading pairs with this accepted line by subject. Reading again cannot remove an accepted line; only a new acceptance can replace the list.

reproposal_restated.plain: The same thing in different words as a line you already accepted. Nothing changes.
reproposal_restated.technical: The paired proposal differs in wording but fails both weakening tests. It is listed so the difference is visible, and it changes nothing.

reproposal_weakened.plain: This new wording says less than the line you already accepted. We are not replacing the stronger one.
reproposal_weakened.technical: The paired proposal either drops a negation the accepted line carries, or its word set is a proper subset of the accepted line's. Both are named as weakenings and neither is applied (`B5.5`).

scope_from_the_work.plain: These are the folders the work already confirmed for this Change touched. Accepting them with what counts as done is what lets later checks be counted for it.
scope_from_the_work.technical: Each entry is the directory of a path one confirmed session changed, spelled as a `dir/**` subtree the scope matcher understands, with entries covered by a shorter one removed. Derived at read from stored rows; nothing on disk is inspected.

scope_none_found.plain: The record does not show which files the work for this Change changed, so there are no folders to cover yet. Confirm the work that belongs to this Change, and they will be proposed here.
scope_none_found.technical: No file-editing tool call with a readable path was found in any confirmed session, so the allowed scope is proposed as empty rather than as the whole project. An empty answer is an answer, never a wildcard.

scope_over_the_bound.plain: {count} more folders were left off this list, which is kept to {version} so it stays something you can read before you accept it.
scope_over_the_bound.technical: The derived entry list exceeded `change_propose::MAX_SCOPE_PATHS`; the remainder is counted here rather than dropped silently. Accepting more is a re-scope with the folders named.

scope_versions_bounded.plain: {lists} of what counts as done so far. We keep at most {version}.
scope_versions_bounded.technical: `COUNT(*)` over this Change's `change_scope_revisions` rows, against `change_propose::MAX_SCOPE_VERSIONS`. Both numbers are shown so the bound is visible before it refuses anything.

type_authorization_sensitive.plain: This work touches who is allowed to do what, so it is worth being careful.
type_authorization_sensitive.technical: A changed path names authorization, a credential or a policy. The profile adds a mandatory static examination; it does not claim the work is unsafe.

type_backend_behaviour.plain: This work changes what the program does behind the screen.
type_backend_behaviour.technical: No changed path matched a narrower kind, so the work is treated as program behaviour and the profile asks for the project's own tests.

type_data_schema.plain: This work changes how stored things are shaped, so what happens to things already stored is part of what counts as done.
type_data_schema.technical: A changed path names a migration, a schema or a `.sql` file. A schema change with no compatibility examination is the one class this product will not read as finished.

type_documentation.plain: This work is mostly writing, not behaviour.
type_documentation.technical: One or more changed paths is a document by extension or directory. `B5.14`: opening a document proves nothing about behaviour.

type_interface_behaviour.plain: This work changes what someone using the product sees or does.
type_interface_behaviour.technical: Changed paths include interface sources or a route. The examinations worth running are the ones that drive the interface, not the ones that read it.
